text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: NovusBank dedicated pool 'nb-prod-pool' entering degraded state. Error rate spike + increased tail latency. Paging #eng-oncall and #customer-success. Severity: P1.

sara.nguyen: on call, looking. saw alerts ~2m ago. pulling metrics now. @paula.ortiz can you flag NovusBank primary contacts?

mike.cho: thx sara. i'm checking pool autoscale and recent deploys to dedicated infra. no deploys in last 30m from CI.

raj.patel: logs show KV cache evictions around 12:02: high mem pressure on 3/6 nodes. some tenants hitting heavy seq2seq workloads.

paula.ortiz: NovusBank CSM on call: @bryan_li (acct exec) is available. They've reported slow responses and a couple of timeouts to their app. Customer facing UX errors ~20% of requests, some 500s. they're monitoring.

bryan_li: I'm with them on the call bridge. They're seeing user-facing failures for a subset of endpoints that map to high-throughput inference routes. Very sensitive to latency.

sara.nguyen: quick mitigation plan: 1) isolate noisy tenant(s) if possible to free pool; 2) attach warm spare nodes (dedicated burst) to nb-prod-pool; 3) fallback routing to compatible hosted model for NovusBank (temp). Starting 1) now.

raj.patel: running tenant throttle script to limit max concurrent sessions for suspected tenant IDs. snippet: ```bash
# throttle by tenant
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/pools/nb-prod-pool/tenants/throttle -d '{"tenant_ids":["t-5883","t-5901"],"concurrency":10}'
```

mike.cho: attached 2 warm nodes (g5x2) to pool; OS-level metrics show memory reclaim but still high. moving one noisy VM to isolate.

incident-bot: Action log: tenant throttle executed by raj.patel at 2063005448. Pool scaled +2 nodes by mike.cho at 2063005452.

paula.ortiz: customer update (on bridge): "NovusBank appreciates fast response. Please escalate — they need ETA and timeline for resolution. Also asked about data separation while we throttle." I'll tell them we're shifting noisy workloads and enabling fallback routing.

bryan_li: customer asks about impact on SLA and potential credit. we should prepare formal note.

raj.patel: mitigation looks effective: 500s dropped from 20% -> 3% in last 3m; p95 latency down ~400ms. continuing monitoring for 15m.

sara.nguyen: handing off to next on-call in 15m. @alex.kim you'll take over if this is still active. I'll prepare quick runbook of actions taken.

alex.kim: ack. joining bridge now, reading up.

mike.cho: root cause hypothesis: a noisy tenant started running long-context generation without KV-cache hints, causing excessive KV cache churn and memory pressure leading to GC-induced tail latencies and some RPC timeouts. Dedicated pool didn't trigger fallback fast enough because autoscale headroom was small.

kelly.legal: note for customer comms: if we propose SLA credit, legal needs exact windows and affected request counts. pls capture time ranges and % of errors.

paula.ortiz: will collect timeline and errors. initial customer-friendly blurb ready: "We've identified a noisy tenant causing resource contention in your dedicated pool. We isolated the tenant and provisioned extra capacity; service has returned to normal. We're preparing a full RCA and remediation plan." any wording changes?

bryan_li: that's good. add: "we are offering a proactive review of your workload patterns and a dedicated optimization session to avoid recurrence."

sara.nguyen: creating incident postmortem draft and RCA in docs: https://docs.internal/incidents/2063005432-rca (draft). Draft includes timeline, metrics, mitigation commands, proposed long-term fixes (better autoscale thresholds, tenant-level QoS, prefetched KV hints).

raj.patel: long-term mitigations: 1) tenant QoS (rate/concurrency limits), 2) KV-cache eviction improvements + soft reservations per tenant, 3) earlier fallback routing if p99 latency > 3s for >2min.

mike.cho: ops follow-up: provision dedicated spare nodes for critical tenants (NovusBank) and review autoscale policies for dedicated pools.

paula.ortiz: next steps for customer comms: 1) send interim incident update (hold), 2) schedule a 30-min postmortem call with NovusBank PMs and infra next week, 3) propose SLA credit amount and remediation plan. I'll prepare email and get approval.

kelly.legal: once we have exact windows, send legal the proposed credit figure and the customer-facing mail for review.

bryan_li: customer asked for exec-level summary. we'll need a 1-pager summarizing impact, root cause, remediation, and credits. I'll draft and loop in @paula.ortiz and @sara.nguyen.

paula.ortiz: drafting interim note now. here's the language I'm planning to send to NovusBank: "We sincerely apologize for the disruption to your service earlier today. Our team isolated a resource-intensive tenant in your dedicated pool and provisioned additional capacity. Service has been restored. We are preparing a full RCA with proposed technical remediations and a compensation proposal for the impacted period." any objections?

sara.nguyen: fine from eng side. add: "we will schedule a technical session to review request patterns and apply optimizations."

alex.kim: handover: I'll keep monitoring for another 2 hours, will escalate to SRE leads if error rate rises above 5% again. update to thread when done.

paula.ortiz: thanks everyone. I'll send the interim customer note in 10m and book the postmortem call for Tue.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status changed to: mitigated at 2063005489. Postmortem required.

sara.nguyen: closing notes: mitigation traced -> throttle + burst capacity + fallback routing. RCA draft link above. action items assigned in the doc.

paula.ortiz: ACTION: send customer interim note (paula), schedule postmortem (paula+bryan), prepare SLA credit calc (kelly + finance), technical review session (mike + raj).

bryan_li: leaving notes for exec update. I'll draft 1-pager and share with paula/kelly.

alex.kim: monitoring stable. no further alerts so far. will post final confirmation at 2063005505.

alex.kim: final: all metrics stable; closing oncall watch.
